title: Reconciliation: LLM-driven contradiction detection with supersession
summary: New pluggable Reconciler protocol detects contradicting facts and soft-supersedes the losing record, distinct from forget().
description:
Add `superseded_by VARCHAR(36)`, `superseded_at TIMESTAMP`, `supersede_reason VARCHAR(255)` (all nullable) to `semantic_facts` (optionally `entity_profiles`/`procedural_memory` too, since those can also go stale) via a new migration. Add a `Reconciler` protocol in `types.py`, parallel in shape to the existing `Consolidator`: `(candidates: list[SemanticFact]) -> list[SupersedeDecision]`, where each decision names a winner id, a loser id, and a reason string (e.g. "contradicts: user now prefers light mode"). Ship a `NoOpReconciler` default, matching the `NoOpConsolidator` pattern. Add `MemoryStore.reconcile(memory_type, scope)` that fetches recent, non-superseded facts for a scope, runs the configured Reconciler, and for each decision sets the loser's `superseded_by`/`superseded_at`/`supersede_reason` — a soft-supersede, NOT a hard delete and NOT a `forget()`-tombstone. Keeping this a distinct field from `deleted_at` matters: it lets an audit trail tell "the user asked us to forget this" apart from "we learned this was contradicted by a newer fact," which is a real governance distinction. Update `list_all()`/`search()` to also exclude `superseded_at IS NOT NULL` rows from normal reads, the same way they already exclude `deleted_at IS NOT NULL` rows.

Inspired by: the Agent Memory Toolkit's reconciliation pass — LLM-driven contradiction detection (not cosine-similarity clustering), with `supersede_reason`/`superseded_by`/`superseded_at` fields recorded on every affected record.

Db2 feasibility: new nullable columns plus a new pluggable protocol following the exact same shape as the existing Consolidator. No new infrastructure. Depends on ENH-1/ENH-2's migration (bundle if practical, or a follow-on migration).

comments.text: Done. Migration 0004_supersession.sql adds superseded_by VARCHAR(36), superseded_at TIMESTAMP, supersede_reason VARCHAR(255) (all nullable) + ix_semantic_facts_superseded_by index to semantic_facts only. entity_profiles and procedural_memory excluded: they are versioned-object tables (update() is the right mechanism for staleness); supersession is meaningful only for semantic_facts which accumulate independently-created atomic claims. Reconciler Protocol + SupersedeDecision @dataclass + NoOpReconciler added to types.py — parallel shape to Consolidator/NoOpConsolidator. SemanticFactRepository extends _SELECT_COLS (now 18 cols: base 15 + 3 supersession), overrides _model_from_row(), and adds supersede(loser_id, winner_id, reason, scope) issuing a scoped UPDATE guarded by AND deleted_at IS NULL AND superseded_at IS NULL. MemoryStore gains reconciler= constructor arg (defaults to NoOpReconciler) and reconcile(memory_type, scope, limit=200) which lists live facts, invokes reconciler, applies each SupersedeDecision via facts.supersede(). list_all() and search() in BaseRepository both now include AND superseded_at IS NULL alongside AND deleted_at IS NULL. create() dedup check also excludes superseded rows (closes the ENH-2 revisit note). 44 new unit tests (test_reconciliation.py). 333 total unit tests pass; ruff clean; mypy strict clean. DECISIONS.md entry and ARCHITECTURE.md section 3 updated.
